Those 11 blocks were the most in a single game by a player in program history. item.title: It’s a bit alarming that Radu Drǎgușin is undroppable
item.description: Not the posture you want your best defender to regularly display. | Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images If you’re a calcio doctor unlucky enough to see your door darkened by a Fiorentina side looking for a diagnosis, you’re in for a long day. I can sum it up by saying that literally everything in the team is broken and shows little evidence of knitting together for more than a week or two at a time. It’s hard to pick a primary symptom in such a shambolic club but it’s time for Paolo Vanoli to consider hooking Radu Drǎgușin. The Romania international was one of the summer’s biggest signings. He followed Fabio Paratici from Tottenham Hotspur to Florence. The deal is structured as a loan that becomes an obligation if he starts an unknown number of games; Spurs would get €25 million plus 10% of any future fee. When he arrived, Dustin George-Miller (my counterpart at Cartilage Free Captain) described it as “our old co-Sporting Director doing us a solid” and that probably should have set some alarm bells ringing. Drǎgușin went straight into the XI under Fabio Grosso and stayed there when Vanoli took over. He was shockingly bad in his first appearances and hasn’t improved much since. His lack of pace and trouble scanning down the line were already well-known and his technical limitations weren’t a secret but he’s also struggled in the areas in which he was supposed to excel. Specifically, he’s lost forwards in the box way too easily. That’s a bad quality in a guy who’s cast as a penalty box defender. It can be difficult to judge defenders because they’re usually most noticeable when somebody upstream of them has made a mistake. For example, Drǎgușin getting cooked in space isn’t great but only happens because a midfielder lost a runner and put him in that situation. The revolving door of defensive partners—Luca Ranieri, Marin Pongračić, Viery—has prevented him from building the relationship that any defensive pairing requires. We also have to account for the Fiorentina Bozo Curse, which infects every defender at the club regardless of profile or status. Allowing for mitigation, though, he just doesn’t look up for it. His struggles with Romania make me think it’s not just a Viola problem. Missing nearly two years with injury has obviously set him well back and his agent Florin Manea spoke over the break about the need for patience, predicting that Drǎgușin wouldn’t hit his stride until February. That’s Manea’s job, of course. He sees his client having a tough time and has tried to ease expectations, also citing the faith Paratici has in a player he’s bought twice before. While the sporting director has faith in Drǎgușin, the question is how much the coach should trust him. Drǎgușin is far from the only problem but hasn’t turned in a mistake-free ninety minutes yet. item.title: ‘Coach killers’ – Cam Skattebo will have Giants teammates feeling different to staff, says Jeff Saturday
item.description: Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo will be the most popular player in the locker room, says Jeff Saturday. But do not expect Giants head coach John Harbaugh to feel the same way. Larger than life personality Cam Skattebo has been a lightning rod for discussion all season, and he encapsulated that in Week 11. After promising never to do his backflip celebration again – due to an innocuous injury to Lions star Aidan Hutchinson while celebrating – Skattebo performed an immediate U-turn on the field after the Giants beat the Jaguars. Speaking to Get Up, analyst and former stand-in Colts head coach Jeff Saturday suggested that the Giants coaching staff will not enjoy working with Skattebo. On the other hand, he believes the Giants players will ‘love’ having Skattebo in the trenches with them. When asked if he would love Skattebo as a teammate, Saturday said: “Coaches don’t love them; players love them. Players love them, coaches hate them, they’re coach killers, so I get it. “But you love a dude like that because he’s going to put his head down and run through a wall for you. “Think about how he finished that drive the other night. I understand he fumbled on the drive before, but it’s that type of guy, they’re great locker room guys. “Listen, this season is long, it’s hard, and you need some relief.” Steve Smith Jr agrees Former NFL wide receiver Steve Smith Jr was in agreement that Cam Skattebo would be a popular locker room guy. He explained: “What Skattebo is, is what you call a tone setter. “Whether you’re down or you’re up, you look to your right or your left, and what do you have? You have a Skattebo.” For all the talk about his personality, Skattebo has been the Giants’ most productive running back this season, with 664 scrimmage yards. But the real frustration has been holding the ball. He has five fumbles this season, and this is what John Harbaugh will be desperate to cut out. item.title: Arteta says Arsenal need more luck to kill off games
item.description: Viktor Gyokeres has scored three goals in all competitions this season for Arsenal. [Getty Images] It might be emerging more as a theme than as a major problem, but in recent weeks Arsenal cannot seem to finish off matches when they are on top. In their past nine outings across all competitions, just once have the Gunners won a game by more than a single goal. The latest frustration came in Tuesday's 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund, though perspective is needed. Arsenal might consider it as two points dropped having gone into half-time ahead, but they remain unbeaten in the current Champions League league phase and have not lost at this stage of the competition for more than two years. But of late, despite dominating large parts of matches, Arsenal have had periods where they have dropped off and allowed opponents back into the game. Against Slavia Prague away in the Champions League, after scoring twice in the first half, Arsenal's standards dropped. The same happened against Newcastle in the Premier League last weekend where they found themselves 2-1 behind in the second half having led at the break, before recovering to eventually draw 2-2. They are producing periods of high-level football, but the struggles to consistently turn that into more goals can lead to nervy finishes. In the draw with Bundesliga leaders Dortmund, Arsenal had 30 shots but just four of those attempts were on target. Boss Mikel Arteta mentioned the failure to capitalise post match, though was keen to praise his side's "brilliant performance". "The way we played, bearing in mind the opposition that we played today and what we've done out there, is just something to be very, very pleased [about] because there is very little more that you can demand from the team," Arteta said. "But obviously, the feeling is that we should reward ourselves much more when you put that kind of performance in the amount of chances (and) situations. "There is an element of luck; there is an element of us finishing the actions better. We need to insist because I think what the team has done and shown today, I think it's the right direction." item.title: Injured Giants starter needs surgery: Here’s how much time he’ll miss (UPDATE)
item.description: UPDATE: The Giants on Tuesday placed Greg Newsome on injured reserve, meaning he must miss at least four games. The soonest he can return is Dec. 28 at the Lions. He will miss important matchups with the Colts, 49ers, Seahawks and Browns. *** Giants cornerback Greg Newsome — who had been thriving — might miss the rest of the regular season. Newsome needs surgery to fix his high right ankle sprain and will be sidelined for four to six weeks, according to NFL reporter Jordan Schultz. Newsome got hurt in Sunday’s huge win over the Jaguars. A four-week recovery window might let him return for the Dec. 28 game at the Lions, after he misses matchups with the Colts, 49ers, Seahawks and Browns. A six-week window could let Newsome return for the regular season finale against the Eagles. After visiting the Lions, the Giants travel to Dallas in Week 17. Of course, the Giants might just win the NFC East — they’re currently in the driver’s seat — and make the playoffs for the first time since 2022. The first weekend of the playoffs is Jan. 16-18. It’s possible — but not guaranteed — that Newsome could come back for that game, presuming the Giants win the division. Newsome and fellow starting outside corner Deonte Banks have both excelled this season. So Newsome’s injury is a big blow to the Giants’ surprisingly successful secondary. On Monday, coach John Harbaugh said Newsome would miss multiple weeks — at the minimum. Harbaugh did not rule out surgery for Newsome. item.title: Niko Kovač ‘happy’ with Borussia Dortmund’s mentality against Arsenal
item.description: Niko Kovač ‘happy’ with Borussia Dortmund’s mentality against Arsenal Niko Kovač has instilled somewhat of a winning mentality into his Borussia Dortmund side this season. With three 1-0 wins in the Bundesliga, his BVB team faced arguably their biggest challenge of the season on Tuesday night when they faced off against Premier League champions and last season’s UEFA Champions League finalists: Arsenal. Although going behind to a superb Viktor Gyökeres wondergoal in the tenth minute, Maximilian Beier equalised for the Bundesliga leaders ten minutes into the second period, before Jobe Bellingham saw his strike ruled out for an offside. Evidently happy with a 1-1 draw in London , Kovač praised his team’s performance. “It’s a big point for us,” Dortmund’s head coach send in his post-match press conference, attended by Get German Football News . “A big moment for all of us, for the team and for the fans who turned out in such large numbers today. “In the end, we’re happy to take the point.” Although Arsenal registered 28 shots, only four were on target. With a pragmatic approach and steely defence, Dortmund are proving difficult to break down. “We’re here in London, so naturally you have to whether the storm. “I think the team showed a really good side of themselves today. You can’t accuse them of hiding or not giving it their all. “We fought as a team, kept fighting back, and showed that we can hold our own against a strong opponent.” GGFN | Daniel Pinder – reporting from the Emirates Stadium

Colts coach Shane Steichen named Richardson the starter after replacing Daniel Jones in the loss to Houston and moving on from Jones. Richardson hadn’t started since Week 16 of 2024. The NFL’s career numbers give the Giants a good reason not to play him like a quarterback who can only hand off: 499 rushing yards and six rushing touchdowns in 11 games that season. New York has a fresh look at what Thibodeaux can give them before a pass. The game book against Jacksonville credits him with stopping Bhayshul Tuten for no gain on a first-quarter run. item.title: Brandon Aiyuk clears waivers, to visit Commanders on Wednesday
item.description: Former San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk cleared waivers on Tuesday morning after being waived by the team this weekend, and it looks like he’s already got his eyes on his next destination. Aiyuk is now scheduled to visit with the Washington Commanders this Wednesday, per ESPN’s Adam Schefter, as he looks to find a new home soon. The Commanders have long been the destination linked to Aiyuk the most, given his relationship with quarterback Jayden Daniels stemming from their time at Arizona State. There is a clear void there for him to fill, as the Commanders, who beat the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday night to improve to 4-5-1, will be without star receiver Terry McLaurin for the rest of the season. If all pans out, Aiyuk could potentially be the team’s ‘X’ wide receiver opposite Antonio Williams, with Stefon Diggs in the slot. However, the Commanders aren’t the only team interested in Aiyuk, according to Schefter, who tweeted that the wide receiver “is expected to draw interest from a few teams, including the Washington Commanders, and would like to sign soon.” Aiyuk has bought a home in the Washington area, so the Commanders obviously seem like the clearest fit. Other potential teams that could logically make sense also include the Pittsburgh Steelers or even the Seattle Seahawks. The 49ers saga with Aiyuk is now officially over, and it looks like he’s going to play this season on another team.

item.title: Friendship with Julio Rodríguez eases Maikel Garcia’s transition to Mariners
item.description: HOUSTON, TX - MAY 14: Kansas City Royals third baseman Maikel Garcia (11) gets high fives from teammates after hitting a home run in the top of the second inning during the MLB game between the Kansas City Royals and Houston Astros at Daikin Park on May 14, 2025 in Houston, Texas. In fact, Garcia said he was so shocked when the call came through from his agent with news about the trade that he actually hung up on him in his surprise. Thankfully, his next call was easier to take. “I was sitting down outside my house, and I was thinking about it – the trade and everything – in my house in Kansas City, and I see my phone receiving a call from Julio,” said Garcia in a Zoom call with Seattle media on Tuesday. “And he just said, ‘ Villano ’ – Villano is my nickname, it means ”the villain” – so he just said, ‘ Villano , what’s going on?’ And I said to him, ‘you knew, and you didn’t tell me anything!’ He said ‘no, bro. I didn’t know anything, but I’m happy that we have you here, and I know the player that you are, and I’m excited to play together. I know the energy that you have, the passion, and that’s going to help me too.’ Because we have the same passion, the same energy, the same – you know, we love to show emotion in the game, and that’s gonna help the team.” “He gave me a lot of confidence.” Garcia is a passionate player, as anyone who watched him on Team Venezuela in this year’s WBC can attest. item.title: Colts add to QB room after cutting Daniel Jones
item.description: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports Colts add to QB room after cutting Daniel Jones appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Indianapolis Colts have added another quarterback to their roster, signing Shane Buechele off the Buffalo Bills’ practice squad on Tuesday. Indianapolis was left with Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard as its only quarterbacks after waiving Daniel Jones last Friday. Head coach Shane Steichen indicated on Monday that the organization intended to bring in another quarterback to address the situation. Buechele’s arrival gives the Colts three quarterbacks again ahead of Sunday’s matchup against the New York Giants. Richardson has been named the starting quarterback moving forward, while Leonard and Buechele will provide additional depth. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Buechele, 28, entered the NFL in 2021 as an undrafted player after his college career at Texas and SMU. He has spent time with both the Kansas City Chiefs and Bills but has appeared in just one regular-season NFL game. That appearance came with the Chiefs during the 2025 campaign versus the Las Vegas Raiders on January 4. He completed seven of 14 passes for 88 yards and added four rushing yards on one carry in a 14-12 defeat. Buechele’s signing was part of several roster adjustments made by Indianapolis on Tuesday. The Colts promoted defensive end Carl Lawson from the practice squad to the 53-man roster and placed rookie defensive end Caden Curry on injured reserve. They also waived veteran offensive tackle Charlie Heck. Additionally, Indianapolis signed veteran offensive tackle Wanya Morris off the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad and brought tight end Sean McKeon and defensive end Cam Sample onto its practice squad. The Colts, who currently hold a 3-8 record, will now prepare for the Giants with Richardson leading the quarterback room and Buechele providing another option. item.description: Peter Casey-Imagn Images NFL Fantasy Football Week 12 2026 Start ‘Em Sit ‘Em: Kicker appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The best fantasy kicker on any given Sunday isn’t always associated with the highest-scoring offense. For example, Washington showcased this reality on Monday night, when its kicker contributed most of the points in a thrilling victory, while some high-powered teams barely had their kickers attempt a field goal. As we enter Week 12, we can expect more of these contrasts, and the busy holiday schedule means lineup decisions need to be made earlier than usual. Instead of chasing after last week’s top scorer, fantasy managers should assess whether an offense can consistently reach scoring opportunities. They should also consider how an opponent manages red-zone drives and when a struggling team might stop relying on field goals altogether. NFL Fantasy Football Week 12 Start ‘Em: Kickers Drew Stevens, Washington Commanders (@ ARI) Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Drew Stevens enters Week 12 with significant momentum after successfully kicking five field goals and one extra point in Washington’s 22-20 victory over Cincinnati. His final kick, a 26-yard field goal as time expired, sealed the win, showcasing his ability to capitalize on multiple scoring opportunities rather than relying on a single long-distance kick. item.title: Mark Pope Buyout: How much it would cost if Kentucky were to fire UK Basketball head coach
item.description: Things aren’t necessarily the greatest in and around Kentucky Basketball right now. It’s year three of the Mark Pope era, and the Wildcats are off to a 4-2 start in 2026, with two losses that have been pretty symbolic. The first loss came in a blowout in Chicago against Kansas in the Champions Classic. Kansas is a program that people nationally can compare Kentucky to; the two programs are at the top of the leaderboard for wins in college basketball history, with Kentucky currently holding a four-game lead. The other layer to that loss is that the man who was leading the Jayhawks that evening in the Windy City chose them over Kentucky. Tyran Stokes, a Louisville native, was down to Kentucky and Kansas before ultimately landing in Lawrence for his presumed one year of college basketball. Following the game, we saw a very telling picture of Pope and Stokes shaking hands, along with some words that circulated on social media. The next loss came to Indiana, at Lucas Oil Stadium last Friday night. An Indiana program that Kentucky fans have pointed fingers at for a long time, making fun of the regression of the Hoosiers basketball program. Many members of Big Blue Nation have used the phrase, “at least we’re not Indiana,” when Kentucky has experienced some low points in recent years. The Hoosier fans still hold on to the Christian Watford shot in 2011, which illustrates how far the mighty have fallen. Now, Kentucky added that loss to its resume. In the two contests, Kentucky allowed 89 points and 90 points, providing zero restriction for the opponent when it comes to scoring the ball. On top of that, Kentucky added a one-point miracle victory against Northern Arizona and a very sloppy win against James Madison. So here we are, with Pope’s first year being a great building block but not incredible, and then a very disappointing year two. This year, he had to prove something, and to this point, he hasn’t. That raises the question: how much would it cost Kentucky to fire the former Wildcat? Well, it ain’t cheap. USA TODAY Network reported that Pope’s contract shows that Kentucky would owe Pope 75% of the $17.25 million left on his contract heading into this season as a buyout. That means the school would owe Pope about $13 million if he’s fired on April 1, 2027. This comes on the heels of Kentucky firing its football coach, Mark Stoops, last December, a move that also came with a hefty price tag. With games against a feisty Wichita State team coming to Rupp Arena this Friday, a road game to Virginia, a home game against Louisville, and a neutral site game in New York against North Carolina, it won’t get much easier anytime soon. Things have been trending downward this season for Kentucky, and if something doesn’t change for the better soon, J Batt may have a decision to make in his first year as the University of Kentucky AD.

item.title: Jim Harbaugh’s ‘Green Dot’ Answer May Be The Nail In The Coffin For Chargers Tenure
item.description: An anonymous NFL executive has predicted that Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh will retire at the end of the 2026 campaign Getty This season has been brutal for the Los Angeles Chargers for so many reasons. The team is 1-9 on the year and to make matters worse head coach Jim Harbaugh just had a confusing answer in a press conference which makes for a really bad look given the team’s struggles. When asked by reporters which defensive player was wearing the “green dot” meaning which player on defense had a radio receiver in his helmet to receive calls from the sidelines, Harbaugh did not know. “Um, a few, I think, uh — who had the green dot? — I’m not for sure. Marlowe Wax, Del’Shawn. Uh, Troy might have had a green dot as well,” he said before asking a staffer who had the green dot. Maybe if the Chargers were having a decent season and were on track to finish 11-6 for a third straight season his answer wouldn’t be so uniformly criticized. Yet, when the team is so bad and coaching has been a major question mark it is just jarring that the coach doesn’t know something that it seems like he should. Harbaugh is not a defensive coach. He was a quarterback in the NFL so obviously he understands that side of the game more, but he should still know what is going on with the defense. Perhaps the fact that he isn’t a playcaller on either side of the ball is why he is not as clued in to what is going on. Do the Chargers need a different style of coach going forward? This controversy really raises the question of what it is that Harbaugh really does. He has refused to take over playcalling duties from offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel even though his tenure has been a trainwreck . He obviously isn’t super invested in what is going on defensively if he doesn’t know the answer to a fairly simple question, so what value is he providing? Clearly, the Chargers thought that he could come in with his track record of success and bring some of that Harbaugh magic to Southern California. Whatever he was doing worked pretty well the last two seasons but going forward one cannot help but wonder whether his head coaching style is what’s best for the Chargers. Someone who knows all the details and is heavily involved, even if they aren’t necessarily calling plays, is what may be needed to get things turned around. The only problem is that the Chargers probably aren’t in a position to fire him given how much money is left on his contract. Perhaps it simply needs to be made clear to him that he needs to be more involved going forward otherwise his job may be in jeopardy should embarrassing episodes like this continue with the product on the field being as bad as it is. item.title: Chiefs Face Worry Over Kenneth Walker Situation Before Thanksgiving Bills Game

Chiefs Running Back Could Have Bigger Problems SI.com’s Joshua Brisco responded to a fan’s question about what the Chiefs might do if Walker is unable to play on Thursday night against the Buffalo Bills. Brisco noted that, while Walker appears to be on track to return, another setback could have long-term implications. “To fully wade into a hypothetical that might be irrelevant by the time Tuesday’s injury report comes out: If Walker doesn’t play in Buffalo, I think you have to have some level of concern about his timeline and expectations for the rest of the year, simply due to the possibility that a short-term injury, downplayed by the team, could be lingering much longer than the player and team expected,” Brisco wrote. “That’s always alarming until the player returns and looks like their pre-injury self.” The Chiefs certainly got some good news on Walker on Tuesday, with the running back returning to practice, but his status for Thursday’s game is far from certain. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid warned that the running back wasn’t expected to do a lot in his return to practice. “We’ll see how he does. I’m not anticipating a ton of work there but he’ll get out there and move around,” Reid said, via reporter Sam McDowell on X . Chiefs May Need to Adjust Gameplan The Chiefs may need to rely heavily on the run game against the Bills, with cold and windy weather in the forecast. Buffalo is expected to get an early winter storm, with wind gusts up to 50 miles per hour late in the evening on Thanksgiving. That could force the Chiefs to hand a bigger workload to rookie running back Emmett Johnson, who has performed well in relief of the injured Walker. Brisco wrote that Johnson appears up the task. “I’ve been hugely impressed by Johnson’s performances throughout the first half of his rookie season, and I think it’s legitimate,” Brisco wrote. “No smoke and mirrors here; he’s a quality NFL back. Rayan Cherki scored an 86th-minute equalizer as City came from behind for a second time to avoid defeat at the hands of the Italians on Tuesday. When you don’t you start questioning everything. “The perfect thing would be to not think but it’s not so easy. “We have so much quality so it’s about getting the quality out in every payer. “We have to regroup, stay positive and bring energy on the pitch and try to do our best.” After a tame first half, City fell behind to a goal from former Manchester United striker Rasmus Hojlund after 55 minutes. Ayyoub Bouaddi pulled them back into the game but City needed to fight back again after Noa Lang restored Napoli’s lead with a fine volley 14 minutes from time. Cherki’s leveller was a fine individual effort but the Frenchman felt the overall performance had been a flat one. He said: “I don’t care about scoring, I just want to win. We played good but we didn’t play with energy, we need to do more. “Today was like the last games, we need to work more.” City manager Enzo Maresca laughed when told of Cherki’s comments, insisting there were positives to build on. The Italian said: “No, I think tonight we pressed very aggressive, we recovered the ball most of the time. Off the ball I think the team was good, from my point of view. “We created a lot of chances but it was difficult. We expected Napoli to play a waiting game in a low block. “We conceded few chances, and the goals we conceded could have been avoided. “There is a degree of regret we didn’t win but when you can’t win, don’t lose. item.title: Justin Turner Reveals Surprising Dodgers Connection During Mexico Championship Run

item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. But it’s not.” Nor is it up to the team’s most loyal supporters, who would like to see someone sacrificed for the team’s fall from grace. item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
